hook_text: Two toothed wheels, one number: divide the teeth and you know the speed, the force and the direction.
clip_script: Two spur gears mesh, teeth pushing teeth, so they turn opposite ways. Always. Ratio is driven teeth over driver teeth. 10 drives 30: 3 to 1, the output turns at a third of the speed with three times the turning force. Flip it, 30 drives 10: three times faster, a third of the force. Speed and force trade; you never get both. Now slip a gear in the middle. The idler flips the direction back to match the driver and changes nothing else; its teeth cancel. Car reverse gear, maize mill. Put two gears on one shaft and the ratios multiply: 3 to 1 then 4 to 1 is 12 to 1.
visual_style: Whiteboard gears with arrows turning opposite ways; tooth counts 10 and 30 with the ratio written; a third gear sliding in and the arrow flipping back; a compound shaft with 3 x 4 = 12.
mood: Quick and numerical, like a puzzle solved.
pacing: Opposite ways, ratio, slow and strong, fast and weak, the idler, the compound.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and cut two cardboard gears with different tooth counts to test the ratio.
